holder-quote: Her eye strayed towards the skeleton, which paused as it brought bowls of Acid Flies out for the Antinium.
It had no will. Skeletons weren’t supposed to have free will. But they weren’t supposed to level either, and the [Skeleton Warrior] was now Level 2.
he was still only a Level 3 [Skeleton Warrior]
Toren was a Level 11 [Skeleton Warrior]. That was his purpose, his name and sense of being.
Toren was a Level 11 [Skeleton Warrior]. That was what the voice in his head told him.
He was currently a Level 14 [Skeleton Warrior], thanks to the battle with the enchanted suit of armor, but that wasn’t nearly good enough.
It was done. He had won. Toren regarded the steaming corpse, and then took a bit of snow and began to clean himself. Erin hated it when he was dirty.
He was a [Skeleton Knight] now? Was that different than a [Skeleton Warrior]?

Az’kerash eyed Toren. Only the skeleton’s head and upper torso were repaired. He had been a basic skeleton, a [Skeleton Warrior]. Now? He was a kind of undead that would have fit among the Village of Dead’s elites—if only the lower echelons.
